title: Nat.lpo_implies_llpo: the limited principle of omniscience yields the lesser limited principle
statement: Written over a Bool-valued sequence f : Nat -> Bool, which is Bishop's formulation: Hits f := exists n, f n = true ("f fires somewhere") and Misses f := forall n, f n = false ("f never fires"). LPO is forall f, Or (Hits f) (Misses f); WLPO is forall f, Or (Misses f) (Not (Misses f)); Markov's principle (MP) is forall f, Not (Misses f) -> Hits f; LLPO is forall f g, Not (And (Hits f) (Hits g)) -> Or (Misses f) (Misses g); EM is forall (P : Prop), Or P (Not P). LLPO is the weak omniscience principle Bishop's school regards as consistent with constructive mathematics, and it is the one this library's analysis boundary certificates keep landing on: creal/ivt_boundary.rs and creal/extreme_value.rs each reduce a classical conclusion to ANALYTIC LLPO (deciding the sign of an arbitrary real), while creal/lub_boundary.rs reaches full excluded middle. Until this family landed, the library had no statement of LLPO to point at. Two nested Or.elims; only the branch where BOTH sequences fire is impossible, and it is refuted by building the forbidden And -- which is exactly why LLPO is weaker than LPO: it never has to say WHICH of the two sequences misses. THE PRINCIPLE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT AN AXIOM. It is spelled out inline in the type -- never behind a Definition -- so a reader of the rendered statement sees the whole assumption and nothing about the conclusion can be smuggled into an abbreviation. That is why axiom_footprint is empty. ADR-1601 (roadmap W0-2) decides this policy and prices it: across the ten theorems of this family the hypothesis route costs 11 binders and 14 argument positions and ZERO proof obligations. WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the principle in its hypothesis is true, false, or independent. The SEPARATIONS in the standard picture -- LPO is not constructively derivable, LLPO does not give LPO, WLPO does not give LPO, MP does not give WLPO -- are CITED here (Bishop, Constructive Analysis ch. 1) and are not proved: each needs a model of this kernel rather than a term in it, and ADR-1600 records why an internal metatheorem about this kernel is unavailable.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.lpo_implies_llpo : ((x0 : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> Or (Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x1 : AxNat) => Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x1) Bool.true)) (((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x1) Bool.false)))) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x3 : Not (And (Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x3 : AxNat) => Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x3) Bool.true)) (Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x3 : AxNat) => Eq.{1} Bool (x2 x3) Bool.true)))) -> Or (((x4 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x4) Bool.false)) (((x4 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x2 x4) Bool.false))))))

evidence.supports: Nat.lpo_implies_llpo is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Nat.lpo_implies_llpo --require-kind theorem
evidence.notes: --require-declaration exits non-zero when the name is absent from every constructed prelude, and --require-kind exits non-zero when it is present with the wrong kind, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the classical principle enters as a HYPOTHESIS and nothing is assumed. Read from Kernel::axiom_footprint, never from a rendered name.
checkers: per-declaration footprint assertion in the suite below
evidence.checker_command: cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib nat_prelude::omniscience -- --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 8 passed'
evidence.notes: The suite's own footprint test reads Kernel::axiom_footprint for every declaration in the family and fails on a non-empty result. The grep -c count is what makes the command discriminating: a fabricated or renamed filter makes cargo print a different passed-count and exit 0, and the anchored pattern then matches nothing, so grep -c prints 0 and exits 1. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. Anchored with [[:space:]]-free literals, never \t -- in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t.

evidence.supports: The statement is the one advertised, not a weaker or stronger one: the theorem is applied at GENUINELY FREE variables of the hypothesis type and the inferred conclusion is pinned against an independently rebuilt term, and a negative control in the hypothesis slot is REQUIRED TO BE REJECTED.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib lpo_implies_llpo_needs_the_disjointness_premise_as_stated -- --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: Numerals reduce and hide definitional-equality gaps, so nothing in this test instantiates a sequence or a real concretely. The builders in the test file are a SECOND, independent implementation of every principle: if they called the module's own private helpers, the check would be comparing a term with itself and could not fail.

notes: Negative control: `Not (And (Misses f) (Misses g))` -- the same term with Hits replaced by Misses in both conjuncts, a small and local change -- must be REJECTED in the premise slot.
